chunks: Al-Ridha عليه السلام wrote to Muhammad ibn Sinan, in what he wrote as a reply to his questions:

The reason a woman does not inherit anything from landed properties except the value of the bricks and demolition materials is that real estate cannot be altered or transformed. A woman may have what is between her and him severed from the bond, and she may be changed and replaced. A child and a parent are not like that, because it is not possible to separate oneself from them, whereas a woman may be replaced. So that which may come and go, its inheritance is in what may be substituted and altered, since it resembles them both; and that which is fixed and enduring in its state is for one who is like it in firmness and permanence.

key_terms.الثَّابِتُ الْمُقِيمُ: that which is fixed and enduring
key_terms.الِاسْتِبْدَالُ بِهَا: replacement in the sense mentioned by the text
key_terms.قِيمَةَ الطُّوبِ وَالنِّقْضِ: the monetary value of bricks and demolition materials

ai.seo_question: Why does a woman not inherit the land itself in this hadith on inheritance law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives the stated legal rationale for a woman's not inheriting the land itself, but only the value of certain building materials, in the context of inheritance law. It contrasts the relative permanence of kinship ties such as child and parent with the marital bond as presented in the text, and explains the ruling on that basis.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5749 - Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha (as) wrote to Muhammad ibn Sinan in response to his questions:

"The reason why a woman does not inherit anything from real estate except for the value of bricks and demolition materials is because real estate cannot be altered or transformed.
A woman may experience a severance of the marital bond, and she herself may change or be replaced. However, a child and a parent are not like that, for separation from them is not possible. A woman, on the other hand, can be replaced. Therefore, what is subject to coming and going, her inheritance is in what can be altered and changed, as it resembles her nature. What is permanent and remains as it is belongs to those who are similar in stability and permanence."
